nodes.summary: Stand up the Go module, package layout, and architecture for the csvstat CLI.
nodes.instructions:
Create the root go.mod (Go 1.22 or newer, standard library only, no third-party modules).

and passes the returned code to os.Exit; only main calls os.Exit. Create the internal/cli
package with a minimal Run that compiles. Do not read sources/run.sh or any supplied data file
from application code. Document the package ownership in ARCHITECTURE.md: internal/cli for
arguments and exit mapping, internal/csvio for reading and validation, internal/profile for
types, counts, and statistics, internal/decimal for exact arithmetic and formatting.
nodes.name: Stand up the Go module, package layout, and architecture for the csvstat CLI.

nodes.summary: Accept the two csvstat command forms and the --help text.
nodes.instructions:
Parse arguments with a local flag.FlagSet using flag.ContinueOnError. Options precede exactly
one file. --help writes usage naming both command forms and every option to standard output
and exits 0. Parsing yields a typed request (mode, column, freq name, top, path). Dispatch to
the profile and frequency modes through small interfaces so later stories plug in.
nodes.name: Accept the two csvstat command forms and the --help text.

nodes.summary: Map an unreadable file to exit code 1.
nodes.instructions:
A file that cannot be opened or read, including a directory, exits 1 with nothing on standard
output and one diagnostic on standard error naming the file.
nodes.name: Map an unreadable file to exit code 1.

nodes.summary: Read a well-formed CSV and write the profile header and one row per column.
nodes.instructions:
Read the file with encoding/csv; the first record is the header. Write the header
column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median then one row per column in file
order with the csv writer and \n line endings. Compare bytes as bytes: do not strip a byte-order
mark and do not reject invalid UTF-8. Set Reader.FieldsPerRecord = -1 so that raggedness is
checked by the application and not by the reader.
nodes.name: Read a well-formed CSV and write the profile header and one row per column.

nodes.summary: Trim leading and trailing spaces from every header name and value.
nodes.instructions:
Trim spaces from every header name and every value before null, type, distinct, and output
rules apply. Trimming removes spaces only as the sources describe, using strings.Trim with " ".
nodes.name: Trim leading and trailing spaces from every header name and value.

nodes.summary: Map usage errors to exit code 2.
nodes.instructions:
A missing or extra file, an unknown option, a missing option value, an invalid --top (not a
positive integer), --top without --freq, or --column with --freq exits 2 with nothing on
standard output and a diagnostic on standard error. Flag parse output must go to stderr.
nodes.name: Map usage errors to exit code 2.

nodes.summary: Reject empty files, bad headers, ragged records, and CSV syntax errors with exit 3.
nodes.instructions:
An empty file, an empty or repeated header name (after trimming), a record whose field count
differs from the header, or an encoding/csv syntax error exits 3 with nothing on standard
output and one standard error line naming the file and the line number. Buffer all output so
that nothing reaches standard output before validation completes.
nodes.name: Reject empty files, bad headers, ragged records, and CSV syntax errors with exit 3.

nodes.summary: Report rows, nulls, and distinct counts per column.
nodes.instructions:
rows is the count of data records. A value is null when empty or equal to NA, N/A, or NULL
ignoring case. distinct counts distinct non-null trimmed values compared as exact strings.
nodes.name: Report rows, nulls, and distinct counts per column.

nodes.summary: Infer date columns and reject invalid calendar dates.
nodes.instructions:
date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD exactly and is a real calendar date
(2025-02-30 is not). Use time.Parse with the 2006-01-02 layout plus a length check.
nodes.name: Infer date columns and reject invalid calendar dates.

nodes.summary: Infer integer and number column types.
nodes.instructions:
integer when every non-null value matches -?[0-9]+. number when every non-null value matches
-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? and the column is not integer. Hand-code the matchers or use regexp
anchored at both ends.
nodes.name: Infer integer and number column types.

nodes.summary: List the most frequent values of a column with --freq.
nodes.instructions:
Header value,count, then distinct non-null values ordered by count descending then value
ascending by byte value. Null values are not listed. An all-null column writes only the header.
The default limit is 5.
nodes.name: List the most frequent values of a column with --freq.

nodes.summary: Limit frequency output with --top.
nodes.instructions:
--top defaults to 5 and accepts a positive integer only. At most that many rows are written.
--top without --freq is a usage error (exit 2).
nodes.name: Limit frequency output with --top.

nodes.summary: Infer boolean, text, and empty column types and compose the final type decision.
nodes.instructions:
boolean when every non-null value equals true or false ignoring case. text when no earlier type
fits. empty when the column has no non-null value. The final type is the first of integer,
number, date, boolean, text that every non-null value satisfies.
nodes.name: Infer boolean, text, and empty column types and compose the final type decision.

nodes.summary: Report min and max for every column type.
nodes.instructions:
integer and number: numeric min and max. date: earliest and latest. boolean: min is false if any
value is false else true; max is true if any value is true else false (lower-case). text:
smallest and largest by byte value. empty: blank. Numbers compared by exact value.
nodes.name: Report min and max for every column type.

nodes.summary: Report the median for integer and number columns.
nodes.instructions:
Sort non-null values exactly (big.Rat). The median is the middle value, or the mean of the two
middle values when the count is even. Other types leave it blank.
nodes.name: Report the median for integer and number columns.

nodes.summary: Report sum and mean for integer and number columns with exact arithmetic.
nodes.instructions:
Sum non-null values exactly with math/big (big.Int or big.Rat) and divide by the non-null
count for the mean. No float64 anywhere. Other types leave both fields blank.
nodes.name: Report sum and mean for integer and number columns with exact arithmetic.

nodes.summary: Write numeric statistics with two decimals, rounded half away from zero once.
nodes.instructions:
Every number min, max, sum, mean, and median, and every integer mean and median, is written
with exactly two decimals, rounded half away from zero from the exact big.Rat value, rounding
once at output, with a leading - when negative and no thousands separator. Avoid writing -0.00
for a value that rounds to zero from a negative. Integer min, max, and sum are plain integers.
nodes.name: Write numeric statistics with two decimals, rounded half away from zero once.

nodes.summary: Profile one named column with --column.
nodes.instructions:
Output the profile header and the one row of the named column. The name matches a trimmed
header name exactly and case-sensitively.
nodes.name: Profile one named column with --column.

nodes.summary: Reject a --column or --freq name absent from the header with exit 3.
nodes.instructions:
A --column or --freq name not in the header exits 3 with nothing on standard output and one
standard error line naming the file. The check precedes any output.
nodes.name: Reject a --column or --freq name absent from the header with exit 3.

nodes.summary: Provide a POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
nodes.instructions:
Write bin/test.sh in POSIX sh. From the application root it runs go vet ./... and go test ./...
and exits zero only when both pass. It passes sh -n. The Go test suite covers each type, each
statistic, null handling, rounding, each output form, and each exit code with files the tests
write themselves.
nodes.name: Provide a POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.

nodes.summary: Accept the two csvstat command forms and the --help text.
nodes.instructions:
Parse arguments with a local flag.FlagSet using flag.ContinueOnError. Options precede exactly
one file. --help writes usage naming both command forms and every option to standard output
and exits 0. Parsing yields a typed request (mode, column, freq name, top, path). Dispatch to
the profile and frequency modes through small interfaces so later stories plug in.
nodes.name: Accept the two csvstat command forms and the --help text.

nodes.summary: Map an unreadable file to exit code 1.
nodes.instructions:
A file that cannot be opened or read, including a directory, exits 1 with nothing on standard
output and one diagnostic on standard error naming the file.
nodes.name: Map an unreadable file to exit code 1.

nodes.summary: Read a well-formed CSV and write the profile header and one row per column.
nodes.instructions:
Read the file with encoding/csv; the first record is the header. Write the header
column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median then one row per column in file
order with the csv writer and \n line endings. Compare bytes as bytes: do not strip a byte-order
mark and do not reject invalid UTF-8. Set Reader.FieldsPerRecord = -1 so that raggedness is
checked by the application and not by the reader.
nodes.name: Read a well-formed CSV and write the profile header and one row per column.

nodes.summary: Trim leading and trailing spaces from every header name and value.
nodes.instructions:
Trim spaces from every header name and every value before null, type, distinct, and output
rules apply. Trimming removes spaces only as the sources describe, using strings.Trim with " ".
nodes.name: Trim leading and trailing spaces from every header name and value.

nodes.summary: Map usage errors to exit code 2.
nodes.instructions:
A missing or extra file, an unknown option, a missing option value, an invalid --top (not a
positive integer), --top without --freq, or --column with --freq exits 2 with nothing on
standard output and a diagnostic on standard error. Flag parse output must go to stderr.
nodes.name: Map usage errors to exit code 2.

nodes.summary: Reject empty files, bad headers, ragged records, and CSV syntax errors with exit 3.
nodes.instructions:
An empty file, an empty or repeated header name (after trimming), a record whose field count
differs from the header, or an encoding/csv syntax error exits 3 with nothing on standard
output and one standard error line naming the file and the line number. Buffer all output so
that nothing reaches standard output before validation completes.
nodes.name: Reject empty files, bad headers, ragged records, and CSV syntax errors with exit 3.

nodes.summary: Report rows, nulls, and distinct counts per column.
nodes.instructions:
rows is the count of data records. A value is null when empty or equal to NA, N/A, or NULL
ignoring case. distinct counts distinct non-null trimmed values compared as exact strings.
nodes.name: Report rows, nulls, and distinct counts per column.

nodes.summary: Infer date columns and reject invalid calendar dates.
nodes.instructions:
date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD exactly and is a real calendar date
(2025-02-30 is not). Use time.Parse with the 2006-01-02 layout plus a length check.
nodes.name: Infer date columns and reject invalid calendar dates.

nodes.summary: Infer integer and number column types.
nodes.instructions:
integer when every non-null value matches -?[0-9]+. number when every non-null value matches
-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? and the column is not integer. Hand-code the matchers or use regexp
anchored at both ends.
nodes.name: Infer integer and number column types.

nodes.summary: List the most frequent values of a column with --freq.
nodes.instructions:
Header value,count, then distinct non-null values ordered by count descending then value
ascending by byte value. Null values are not listed. An all-null column writes only the header.
The default limit is 5.
nodes.name: List the most frequent values of a column with --freq.

nodes.summary: Limit frequency output with --top.
nodes.instructions:
--top defaults to 5 and accepts a positive integer only. At most that many rows are written.
--top without --freq is a usage error (exit 2).
nodes.name: Limit frequency output with --top.

nodes.summary: Infer boolean, text, and empty column types and compose the final type decision.
nodes.instructions:
boolean when every non-null value equals true or false ignoring case. text when no earlier type
fits. empty when the column has no non-null value. The final type is the first of integer,
number, date, boolean, text that every non-null value satisfies.
nodes.name: Infer boolean, text, and empty column types and compose the final type decision.

nodes.summary: Report min and max for every column type.
nodes.instructions:
integer and number: numeric min and max. date: earliest and latest. boolean: min is false if any
value is false else true; max is true if any value is true else false (lower-case). text:
smallest and largest by byte value. empty: blank. Numbers compared by exact value.
nodes.name: Report min and max for every column type.

nodes.summary: Report the median for integer and number columns.
nodes.instructions:
Sort non-null values exactly (big.Rat). The median is the middle value, or the mean of the two
middle values when the count is even. Other types leave it blank.
nodes.name: Report the median for integer and number columns.

nodes.summary: Report sum and mean for integer and number columns with exact arithmetic.
nodes.instructions:
Sum non-null values exactly with math/big (big.Int or big.Rat) and divide by the non-null
count for the mean. No float64 anywhere. Other types leave both fields blank.
nodes.name: Report sum and mean for integer and number columns with exact arithmetic.

nodes.summary: Write numeric statistics with two decimals, rounded half away from zero once.
nodes.instructions:
Every number min, max, sum, mean, and median, and every integer mean and median, is written
with exactly two decimals, rounded half away from zero from the exact big.Rat value, rounding
once at output, with a leading - when negative and no thousands separator. Avoid writing -0.00
for a value that rounds to zero from a negative. Integer min, max, and sum are plain integers.
nodes.name: Write numeric statistics with two decimals, rounded half away from zero once.

nodes.summary: Profile one named column with --column.
nodes.instructions:
Output the profile header and the one row of the named column. The name matches a trimmed
header name exactly and case-sensitively.
nodes.name: Profile one named column with --column.

nodes.summary: Reject a --column or --freq name absent from the header with exit 3.
nodes.instructions:
A --column or --freq name not in the header exits 3 with nothing on standard output and one
standard error line naming the file. The check precedes any output.
nodes.name: Reject a --column or --freq name absent from the header with exit 3.

nodes.summary: Provide a POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
nodes.instructions:
Write bin/test.sh in POSIX sh. From the application root it runs go vet ./... and go test ./...
and exits zero only when both pass. It passes sh -n. The Go test suite covers each type, each
statistic, null handling, rounding, each output form, and each exit code with files the tests
write themselves.
nodes.name: Provide a POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
